learning: Iteration 2 showed zero line losses did not stop off-track exits at about 6 cm max_error, so the lead and the gains are the remaining suspects. Measure progress, max_error, line losses and steering_oscillation on all three development tracks.
notes: Robot package for the Builder's single-variable test: iteration 1 geometry with the lead moved from 4 cm to 2 cm. Gains are kept from iteration 1 so the lead is the only change.
rationale: Iteration 1 (±3 cm span, 4 cm lead, 12 mm footprints, 0.6 kg, 0.11 m track) remains the best design, scoring 51.27 with line losses at 1 per run. Iteration 2 (±6 cm, 16 mm footprints, 3 cm lead) cut line losses to 0 but still ended every run off track at max_error about 0.06 m, and s-bend progress fell to 4%. So span and footprint are not the limit, and line losses are not the cause of the exit. The Builder's single-variable test moves the lead from 4 cm to 2 cm on the iteration 1 geometry. I keep that geometry (±3 cm, five sensors at 1.5 cm pitch, 12 mm footprints, 0.6 kg, 0.11 m track, 0.03 m wheel radius) and change only the lead. The weights stay [-2,-1,0,1,2], which is the left-positive ordering used in iteration 1. kp 3.0 and ki 0 carry over unchanged. kd stays at 0.1, not the 0.15 used in iteration 2, because the iteration 1 array is the one being tested and kd was not the variable under study. base_speed 1.6 and line_loss 'last_direction' are unchanged. Expected result, not measured: progress above 0.15 on the s-bend and 0.11 on the oval, and max_error below 0.06 m if the lead is the limit. If progress falls or line losses rise, the lead is too close and the next step is to restore 4 cm and test sensor_size 0.016 alone.
